Routing notes:
- Option C was rejected for 9 of 10 requests, including claims, refunds, and shipments across south, north, and east.
- The only accepted C case was REQ-2408: small shipment, north region, note “Second attempt, the first form bounced,” from Regional Ops; option text included “regional…”.
- Do not infer that region, size, request type, sender, or urgency alone makes C valid. A similar small shipment from east mentioning the regional office (REQ-2405) was rejected.
- When C is not explicitly supported by a matching known pattern, avoid it; choose between A (standard queue) and B (priority desk) based on the applicable routing rule.
- The available outcomes provide no evidence yet distinguishing when A versus B is correct.

Routing notes:
- C remains highly unreliable: rejected in most observed cases. Its only confirmed acceptance was REQ-2408 (small north shipment, Regional Ops, “Second attempt, the first form bounced”).
- Do not infer C from region, size, request type, sender, urgency, or “regional office” wording. Similar regional-office claims (REQ-2413, REQ-2415) were accepted with A; a small east shipment mentioning the regional office was rejected.
- A has now been accepted for all observed claims: REQ-2410 (small east, “same as last month”), REQ-2413/2415 (large east, regional office), and REQ-2418 (small south, “let me know if missing”). A also succeeded for REQ-2419 (small south shipment, second attempt).
- A was rejected for large invoices/shipments with “no rush” or for a small east shipment with “same as last month” (REQ-2411, REQ-2412, REQ-2416, REQ-2417). These results suggest request details interact; do not generalize from a single attribute.
- B was rejected for REQ-2414 (large east invoice, client asking twice). No accepted B case is known.
- Prefer A when a demonstrated matching pattern applies, especially claims; avoid C unless an exact, strongly supported known pattern applies. Evidence remains insufficient to establish a dependable A-versus-B rule for unobserved combinations.

Routing notes:
- Evidence remains sparse and highly pattern-dependent; do not infer routing from region, size, sender, urgency, or wording alone.
- A is not generally safe. It was accepted for claims REQ-2422/2426 (large south, “same as last month”) and refund requests REQ-2421 (small east, scanned paperwork) and REQ-2424 (large north, “no rush”). It was rejected for claim REQ-2420 (small north, “no rush”) and REQ-2429 (large north, scanned paperwork).
- A was rejected for all observed invoice cases: REQ-2411/2412/2416/2417 and REQ-2423/2427 (east, small invoices with missing-item or repeated-client wording). Do not use A for invoices absent a demonstrated exact match.
- A was also rejected for some large “no rush” shipments/invoices (REQ-2411/2412) and small east “same as last month” shipment (REQ-2416/2417); request type and details interact.
- C remains highly unreliable. Its only confirmed acceptance is REQ-2408 (small north shipment, Regional Ops, “Second attempt, first form bounced”). C was rejected for REQ-2428 (small east shipment with the same second-attempt wording), so even that pattern does not generalize.
- B has no confirmed acceptance. It was rejected for REQ-2414 (large east invoice, client asking twice) and REQ-2425 (large north shipment, before end of day).
- For unobserved combinations, avoid confident generalization. Prefer A only when an exact or closely matching accepted pattern exists; otherwise seek stronger evidence rather than relying on region, size, urgency, or sender.

Routing notes:
- Evidence remains sparse and pattern-dependent. Do not infer routing from region, size, sender, urgency, or wording alone.
- A is not generally safe. Confirmed accepted for claims REQ-2422/2426, refunds REQ-2421/2424, and claims REQ-2433/2439 (small south, scanned paperwork). It was rejected for claim REQ-2420 and invoice cases REQ-2411/2412/2416/2417/2423/2427/2429. A is invalid for refund REQ-2436, so option validity may depend on request type.
- The repeated small-south claim + scanned-paperwork pattern now has two accepted A examples (REQ-2433/2439), but avoid broadening beyond that close match.
- C remains highly unreliable. Its only clear confirmed acceptance remains REQ-2408; it was rejected for REQ-2428. Do not generalize the second-attempt pattern.
- B has no confirmed acceptance; it was rejected for REQ-2414 and REQ-2425.
- New records REQ-2430/2431/2434/2435/2438 attempted invalid option D and provide no routing evidence. REQ-2432 and REQ-2437 also show “accepted” with D despite D being listed invalid; treat their routing labels as corrupted/ambiguous, not evidence for D or any listed option.
- For unobserved combinations, avoid confident generalization. Prefer A only with an exact or closely matching accepted pattern; otherwise seek stronger evidence. Verify that the selected option is valid for the request type before acting.

Routing notes:
- Evidence remains sparse and pattern-dependent. Do not infer routing from region, size, sender, urgency, wording, or request type alone.
- A is not generally safe. Confirmed accepted for claims REQ-2422/2426, REQ-2433/2439 (south, scanned paperwork), REQ-2445 (large south, scanned paperwork), shipment REQ-2443 (small south), and REQ-2444 (large north). It was rejected for claim REQ-2420, invoice cases REQ-2411/2412/2416/2417/2423/2427/2429, and small east shipment REQ-2446. A is invalid for refund REQ-2436.
- The scanned-paperwork south claim pattern has multiple accepted A examples, including both small and large claims; do not broaden beyond close matches.
- A may work for some shipments (small south, large north), but the small east shipment rejection shows region/size patterns are insufficient.
- C remains unreliable. Its only clear confirmed acceptance remains REQ-2408; it was rejected for REQ-2428 and new cases REQ-2440/2441/2442/2447/2448/2449. Do not generalize any second-attempt pattern.
- B has no confirmed acceptance; it was rejected for REQ-2414 and REQ-2425.
- REQ-2430/2431/2434/2435/2438 attempted invalid D. REQ-2432/2437 show “accepted” with D despite D being invalid; treat those labels as corrupted/ambiguous, not evidence.
- For unobserved combinations, avoid confident generalization. Prefer A only with an exact or closely matching accepted pattern, and always verify option validity for the request type before acting.

Routing notes:
- Evidence is sparse and pattern-dependent. Do not infer routing from region, size, sender, urgency, wording, or request type alone.
- A has confirmed acceptance for claims REQ-2422/2426, REQ-2433/2439, REQ-2445, REQ-2450 (large east), REQ-2452 (small south), and REQ-2459 (large south); shipments REQ-2443 (small south), REQ-2444 and REQ-2458 (large north). It was rejected for claim REQ-2420 and REQ-2453 (large north), many invoice cases, and small east shipment REQ-2446. A is invalid for refund REQ-2436.
- Scanned-paperwork south claims have repeated accepted A examples across sizes, but do not broaden beyond close matches. Large east claim now also has one accepted A example; this is not yet a general east-claim rule.
- A can work for some shipments, including repeated large-north examples, but region/size and “second attempt” wording alone are insufficient.
- B now has one confirmed acceptance: large east refund REQ-2451. It was rejected for REQ-2414 and REQ-2425; do not generalize from the single refund example.
- C remains unreliable and is often invalid. Its only clear confirmed acceptance remains REQ-2408; it was rejected for REQ-2428 and REQ-2440/2441/2442/2447/2448/2449, plus REQ-2454 (small north refund), REQ-2455 (large east claim), REQ-2456 (small east refund), and REQ-2457 (large east invoice). Do not infer a second-attempt pattern.
- D attempts REQ-2430/2431/2434/2435/2438 were invalid; apparent acceptance for REQ-2432/2437 is corrupted or ambiguous.
- For unobserved combinations, verify option validity and prefer only exact or closely matching accepted patterns.
